title: SOFR Rate Snapshot - April 21, 2026

source.name: FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)

summary: SOFR closed at 3.63% on April 21, 2026, unchanged from the prior day. The rate has declined 9 basis points over the past week from 3.72% on April 15 to 3.63% on April 21.
key_points: Direction: flat (0 bps change from prior day)
Decline of 9 bps over the past week
why_it_matters: SOFR is the primary overnight reference rate for U.S. dollar markets, used as the benchmark for trillions of dollars in derivatives, loans, and floating-rate instruments. Tracking daily SOFR levels provides real-time insight into short-term funding conditions and money market stress.
market_structure_context: SOFR is derived from overnight Treasury reverse repurchase agreements collateralized by Treasury securities. The flat reading suggests stable overnight funding markets with no acute stress in the repo market.
notes: This is a pure data observation with no analytical content. The record captures the current SOFR level but provides no context for interpretation. For research purposes, this serves as a time-series anchor point. The flat reading is notable in context of the prior week's declining trend, suggesting stabilization near 3.63%. However, without accompanying FOMC or money market commentary, the macro significance is indeterminate.
